name: Women's Street Safety in Wuhan: Pairwise Comparison
description:
Method replication: participants compare pairs of street views from central Wuhan and pick the one where they would feel safer, with a lower chance of experiencing violence, or choose Equal; the images are not the paper's stimuli (114 re-fetched Baidu street views, one of four cardinal directions per point, 2016–2022).

Original study: Chen, Lin, Yao & Zhou (2024), Land 13(12), 2108. Tencent Street View images from 2018 in four cardinal directions at sampling points along OSM roads in Wuhan's seven central districts. Thirty-one female volunteers aged 18–30 each compared 73 pairs (about 30 minutes) in the authors' software, choosing left, equal or right on women's perceived safety. The choices trained a Gist + RankNet ranking model, and FCN-8s segmentation features were related to the scores with OLS and GWR.

Differences from the original study: (1) Baidu street views instead of the authors' 2018 Tencent images; (2) pairs are drawn at random from 114 images rather than the authors' sample; (3) gender and age are asked so the template can be shared with anyone and filtered to women aged 18–30 as in the paper; the ranking model and regressions are not part of the survey.
author: Chen, Lin, Yao & Zhou
